topic.angle: A provably unsolvable problem in computing

card.title: Some questions no program can answer

body.claim: No single program can tell, for every other program, whether it will finish or run forever.
body.why: This is the halting problem: given a program and an input, decide whether it eventually halts or runs forever. Alan Turing proved in 1937 that no general algorithm can solve it for all program-input pairs. A proof by contradiction supposes such a checker exists and shows that leads to nonsense.

probes.question: What does the halting problem ask?
options: Whether a program will finish or run forever

probes.question: True or false: Turing proved that one algorithm can decide the halting problem for every program and input.

claims.claim: Halting problem: decide whether a program halts or runs forever
claims.quote: determining whether said program will eventually finish running and halt, or will continue to run forever

claims.claim: Turing proved in 1937 that no general algorithm solves it for all program-input pairs
claims.quote: Alan Turing proved in 1937 that the halting problem is undecidable
claims.note: Same passage: no general algorithm exists that can correctly solve the problem for all possible program-input pairs.

claims.claim: The proof is by contradiction, supposing such a checker exists
claims.quote: Christopher Strachey outlined a proof by contradiction that the halting problem is not solvable.
